name: Google Compute Engine
description: Enables you to agentically manage your cloud compute infrastructure spanning deployment and operations.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Google Compute Engine to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Google Compute Engine to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://compute.googleapis.com/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Google Compute Engine MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google Compute Engine lists 29 MCP tools, including create_instance, delete_instance, start_instance, stop_instance, reset_instance, get_instance_basic_info, set_instance_machine_type, list_instance_attached_disks, list_instances, get_instance_group_manager_basic_info, list_instance_group_managers, and list_managed_instances.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Google Compute Engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Google Compute Engine in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and Celesto Cloud Computers.

_published_faq.name: Does Google Compute Engine MCP require authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google Compute Engine requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
Google Compute Engine is developed by Google. It is listed as partner on the Claude connector directory.
